sections.title: En or ett: every thing has a partner
body: Every Swedish noun belongs to one of two groups: en words and ett words. This is called noun gender. En and ett are articles: both mean a or an. En dator is a computer; ett jobb is a job. The group matters later too: it decides the word for “the” and the ending of describing words (Lecture 5).

The word itself rarely shows its group, so learn the article together with the noun. Most nouns, roughly 75–80%, are en words, so en is the better guess when you are not sure. Words for people are usually en words: en kvinna, en läkare. A useful exception is ett barn (a child).

Some endings give a clue. Nouns that end in -a are nearly always en words: en lista, en vecka (exceptions: ett öga, an eye; ett hjärta, a heart). Nouns that end in -are, -ing or -het are en words too: en lärare, en tidning (a newspaper), en frihet (freedom). Nouns that end in -um are ett words: ett museum, ett gymnasium.

A compound word is two words joined into one. The last part decides the gender. Dator is an en word, but spel is an ett word, so datorspel is an ett word: ett datorspel. Lista is an en word, so önskelista is too: en önskelista.

Hindi and Marathi give nouns a gender too, but en and ett are not male and female: en pojke (a boy) and en flicka (a girl) are both en words. They also have no articles (no a or the), so it is easy to leave en or ett out. Say it each time you name one thing: Det är en dator, not Det är dator. (A few fixed phrases have none: söker jobb, spelar piano.)

sections.title: Work: what you do and where
body: Ask Vad jobbar du med? (What do you do for work?). The answer usually uses jobbar som plus the job: Jag jobbar som lärare. Do not put en or ett before the job, not even after är: Jag är lärare. English says a teacher, so Jag är en lärare is the classic slip. (With a describing word, en comes back: en bra lärare.) Jobbar already means work or am working, so never say Jag är jobbar, just as Jag pluggar in Lecture 3.

Use jobbar på plus the workplace. The workplace keeps its article: på en skola, på ett sjukhus, på ett kontor i stan (in town). A company name needs no article: på Ikea. Arbetar means the same as jobbar; it is a little more formal.

Hemifrån (from home) and mestadels (mostly) are adverbs: they say where from and how much. På distans means remotely. To name your field, use inom: Jag jobbar inom IT. Not working at the moment? Say Jag studerar (or Jag pluggar, Lecture 3) or Jag söker jobb (I am looking for a job).

examples.note: No article after är with a profession either.

examples.fi: Jag jobbar på ett företag i Finland.
examples.en: I work at a company in Finland.

sections.title: Free time: what do you do?
body: The teacher’s homework question is Vad gör du på fritiden? (What do you do in your free time?). Answer with a verb in the present tense: Jag läser en bok. Jag lyssnar på musik. Jag tränar på gymmet.

English uses play for everything. Swedish has two verbs. Spelar is for games, sports and instruments: spelar datorspel, spelar fotboll, spelar piano. Leker is free play, the way children and pets play: leker med min katt.

Some free time is at home: stannar hemma (stay at home), vilar (rest), lagar mat (cook). Some is away: åker till havet (go to the sea), solar (sunbathe), badar (swim for fun), åker till fjällen (go to the mountains), åker skidor (ski), reser utomlands (travel abroad), går på bio (go to the cinema). Går en kurs means takes a course: en språkkurs, en matlagningskurs. In Finland, many people also bastar (take a sauna); you will hear går i bastu too.

Semester is a holiday from work (not a school term): Jag har semester or Jag är på semester. Fikar means having coffee and something sweet. Swedes say it all the time; in Finland, Swedish speakers usually say dricker kaffe.

Leker: free play with a child or a pet.

sections.title: Habits: brukar and time phrases
body: Brukar means usually: it says that something is a habit. It works like the help verbs in Lecture 3 (kan, vill, ska). Brukar is the present-tense verb, and the next verb stays in the infinitive (the basic form), with no att: brukar läsa, not brukar läser or brukar att läsa. Careful: brukar is not English used to, which is about the past. Jag brukar läsa means I usually read, now.

Word order works as in Lecture 3. A time phrase can come first; then the verb comes second and the subject after it: På helgen brukar jag läsa, not På helgen jag brukar läsa. Inte goes right after the first verb: Jag brukar inte träna. På helgen brukar jag inte träna.

Useful time phrases: på fritiden (in your free time), på helgen (at the weekend), på morgonen (in the morning), på eftermiddagen (in the afternoon), på kvällen (in the evening) and då och då (now and then, the same as ibland). Så fort som möjligt means as soon as possible.

Watch the small preposition before the time. På + kvällen, helgen, morgonen often describes a habit: på kvällen = in the evening, any evening. I + the time points to one particular time: i kväll = tonight, i helgen = this weekend. A trap: i morgon (Lecture 3) means tomorrow; in the morning is på morgonen. In Finland you will often hear på veckoslutet instead of på helgen; both are correct.

examples.en: At the weekend I usually read a book.
examples.note: Time first, then brukar, then jag.

items.why: På kvällen = in the evening, any evening: På kvällen brukar jag läsa.
I kväll = tonight, this one evening: I kväll går jag på bio.
På helgen = at the weekend, every weekend: På helgen brukar jag vila.
I helgen = this weekend: Vill du gå på bio i helgen?
I morgon = tomorrow (Lecture 3). In the morning is på morgonen.
På morgonen = in the morning, as a habit: På morgonen tränar jag.
Då och då = now and then: again and again, like ibland.
Varje dag = every day (Lecture 3): Du pluggar varje dag.

activities.summary: På + kvällen/helgen/morgonen often describes a habit. I kväll, i helgen and i morgon point to one particular time.

pronunciation.text: lärare, läkare, bokförare, datorspel, önskelista. Ingenjör, servitör, advokat, programmerare. Jag jobbar som ingenjör.
pronunciation.tip: Stress first, as in Lecture 1. Swedish-made words and compound words stress the first part: LÄ-rare, LÄ-kare, BOK-förare, DA-torspel, ÖN-skelista. Many job words are loanwords that stress the end, like ka-FÉ: ingen-JÖR, servi-TÖR, advo-KAT, program-ME-rare. In lärare and datorspel the Sweden-Swedish voices add a second, sing-song tone. Finland-Swedish has no such tone, so you do not need it: just stress the right syllable.

assignment.title: Episode 4 mission: My work and free time
assignment.instructions:
CORE: Say five lines: what you do, where you do it, how you work, and two free-time habits. Use brukar for at least one habit and a time phrase such as på helgen.

WRITE: Send your 25–45 word email to your new språkvän, with one question. Check that som + profession has no article.

RETURN: Tomorrow, say your work or study line and two habits without looking.
assignment.model: Jag jobbar som programmerare. Jag jobbar på ett företag i Helsingfors, men jag jobbar mestadels hemifrån. På helgen brukar jag läsa en bok. På kvällen lyssnar jag på musik. Då och då går jag på bio.

takeaways: Learn a noun with its article: en dator, ett jobb. Most nouns are en words, and endings help (-a, -ing, -are: en; -um: ett). The last part decides a compound word: ett datorspel.
Work: jobbar som + profession, with no article (not som en lärare); jobbar på + workplace, with its article.
Free time: spelar for games, sports and instruments; leker for free play with children and pets.
Habits: brukar + infinitive, with no att, like kan and vill. Put a time first and keep the verb second: På helgen brukar jag läsa. På helgen = every weekend; i helgen = this weekend.
